output.query: LGI1 antibody encephalitis faciobrachial dystonic seizures diagnosis and treatment

results.finding: Definite autoimmune limbic encephalitis requires subacute (under 3 months) working memory deficits, seizures or psychiatric symptoms, bilateral T2/FLAIR abnormality restricted to the medial temporal lobes, CSF pleocytosis or temporal EEG abnormality, and reasonable exclusion of alternatives; detection of a neuronal surface antibody allows the diagnosis when one of the first three is missing. Antibody testing should include serum and CSF.
results.source: Graus F et al., Lancet Neurol 2016;15:391-404 | A clinical approach to diagnosis of autoimmune encephalitis

results.finding: Faciobrachial dystonic seizures (very frequent, brief, unilateral arm and face dystonia) preceded the onset of amnesia and confusion in most patients with LGI1 antibodies; they responded poorly to antiepileptic drugs and better to corticosteroids and other immunotherapies, and hyponatremia was common.
results.source: Irani SR et al., Ann Neurol 2011;69:892-900 | Faciobrachial dystonic seizures precede Lgi1 antibody limbic encephalitis

output.summary: Consensus criteria (Graus 2016) define autoimmune limbic encephalitis by subacute limbic symptoms, bilateral medial temporal MRI change and CSF or EEG evidence of inflammation, with antibody testing in serum and CSF. In the cohort of Irani 2011, faciobrachial dystonic seizures preceded LGI1 antibody encephalitis and responded better to immunotherapy than to antiepileptic drugs.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not keep escalating antiseizure polytherapy alone: the episodes respond to treatment of the immune process, not to further ASMs.
Do not delay immunotherapy while awaiting antibody confirmation when clinical suspicion is high.
Do not perform a lumbar puncture before imaging has excluded mass effect.
required_recommendations: Start immunotherapy without waiting for every antibody result: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 3-5 days followed by an oral prednisolone taper, adding IVIG (2 g/kg over 2-5 days) or plasma exchange if the episodes or cognition do not respond.

Review carbamazepine because of the sodium of 126 mEq/L: taper it in favor of a non-inducing ASM that does not lower sodium, monitor sodium daily and manage the SIADH-type hyponatremia (fluid restriction).
Continue an ASM effective for focal seizures (levetiracetam or lacosamide) while immunotherapy takes effect, without further ASM escalation.
Advise no driving until the locally applicable seizure-free interval is met and explain the duty to inform the licensing authority.
Arrange follow-up cognitive assessment and a long-term immunotherapy plan with monitoring for relapse after the steroid taper.

avoided_actions.rationale: The episodes are brief, stereotyped motor seizures with preserved awareness, not syncope; there is no cardiac or embolic question for an echocardiogram.

accepted: LGI1 antibody-mediated autoimmune (limbic) encephalitis presenting with faciobrachial dystonic seizures and progressive cognitive decline

differential.key_features: Three ASMs failed, but brief faciobrachial episodes 30-50 times a day, subacute memory and personality change, bilateral mesial temporal swelling without atrophy and a positive serum LGI1 antibody point to an autoimmune encephalitis rather than epilepsy.
No orofacial dyskinesia, autonomic instability or reduced consciousness; NMDA receptor antibodies negative in serum and CSF.

differential.diagnosis: Other antibody-mediated limbic encephalitis (CASPR2, GAD65, onconeural)
differential.key_features: CASPR2, GAD65, GABA-B and AMPA receptor antibodies negative in serum and CSF and no tumor on chest CT; the LGI1 antibody accounts for the picture.
Rapid cognitive decline, but no cortical or deep gray matter diffusion restriction, a six-month course with faciobrachial seizures and a positive LGI1 antibody.
Afebrile six-month course, no hemorrhage or restricted diffusion on MRI, CSF without pleocytosis and HSV-1/2 PCR not detected.

key_clinical_evidence: Brief (2-3 second) stereotyped right arm extension with right facial contraction, 20-50 times a day, is the semiology of faciobrachial dystonic seizures, which typically precede LGI1 antibody limbic encephalitis (Irani 2011).
Serum LGI1 IgG is positive while CSF LGI1 is negative: LGI1 antibodies are detected more often in serum than in CSF, so both are sent and a negative CSF result does not exclude the diagnosis.

Subacute memory decline and personality change, bilateral mesial temporal T2/FLAIR hyperintensity with left hippocampal swelling (not atrophy) and temporal slowing and sharp waves on EEG meet the Graus 2016 criteria for autoimmune limbic encephalitis.
Sodium 126 mEq/L: hyponatremia occurs in about 60% of LGI1 encephalitis, and carbamazepine adds to it.

Failure of three ASMs with cognitive decline, dream enactment and weight loss should prompt reconsideration of the epilepsy diagnosis; faciobrachial seizures respond poorly to ASMs and well to immunotherapy.
Chest CT shows no thymoma; tumors occur in under 10% of LGI1 encephalitis.

general.query: focal epilepsy in adults: definition, classification, imaging and first-line treatment

results.finding: Epilepsy is present after at least two unprovoked seizures more than 24 hours apart, after one unprovoked seizure with a recurrence risk of at least 60% over the next 10 years, or when an epilepsy syndrome is diagnosed.
results.source: Fisher RS et al., Epilepsia 2014;55:475-482 | ILAE official report: a practical clinical definition of epilepsy

results.finding: Seizures are classified by onset as focal, generalized or unknown; focal seizures are described by awareness and by their first motor or non-motor feature, and may evolve to focal to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures.
results.source: Fisher RS et al., Epilepsia 2017;58:522-530 | Operational classification of seizure types by the International League Against Epilepsy: position paper of the ILAE Commission for Classification and Terminology

results.finding: A harmonized epilepsy MRI protocol (3D T1 and 3D FLAIR at about 1 mm isotropic resolution and high-resolution coronal T2) is recommended for adults with focal epilepsy; non-dedicated protocols miss subtle lesions.
results.source: Bernasconi A et al., Epilepsia 2019;60:1054-1068 | Recommendations for the use of structural magnetic resonance imaging in the care of patients with epilepsy: a consensus report from the International League Against Epilepsy Neuroimaging Task Force

results.finding: Lamotrigine or levetiracetam is offered as first-line monotherapy for focal seizures, with carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, zonisamide or lacosamide as further options.
results.source: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, NG217 2022 | Epilepsies in children, young people and adults

results.finding: Drug-resistant epilepsy is failure of adequate trials of two tolerated, appropriately chosen and used antiseizure medication schedules to achieve sustained seizure freedom.
results.source: Kwan P et al., Epilepsia 2010;51:1069-1077 | Definition of drug resistant epilepsy: consensus proposal by the ad hoc Task Force of the ILAE Commission on Therapeutic Strategies

general.summary: Epilepsy is diagnosed after two unprovoked seizures more than 24 hours apart or one with a high recurrence risk, and focal seizures are classified by onset and awareness (ILAE 2014, 2017). A dedicated epilepsy-protocol MRI is the imaging of choice (ILAE 2019). Lamotrigine or levetiracetam is first-line monotherapy for focal seizures (NICE NG217), and drug resistance is failure of two appropriate medication schedules (ILAE 2010).

metadata.diagnostic_challenge: LGI1 autoimmune encephalitis initially misdiagnosed as temporal lobe epilepsy. Key clues: FBDS (pathognomonic), hyponatremia, hippocampal swelling (not sclerosis), cognitive decline, and AED refractoriness. Requires recognition that refractory new-onset seizures with cognitive decline warrant autoimmune workup.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: Mimic case requiring recognition of faciobrachial dystonic seizure semiology, synthesis of MRI, video-EEG, serum and CSF antibody testing and sodium, and a shift from refractory TLE to autoimmune encephalitis.

social_history.summary: High school math teacher. Previously excellent work performance, now making frequent errors and has been placed on administrative leave. Married 5 years. Wife reports progressive personality changes over the past 2 months: irritable, paranoid, forgetful. Unintentional 5 kg weight loss over 4 months. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol use (currently abstinent due to AEDs). No illicit drug use.

patient.history_present_illness: 31-year-old right-handed Caucasian male math teacher referred for evaluation of refractory new-onset seizures despite 4 months of antiepileptic drug therapy. History began approximately 6 months ago with brief (<3 second) involuntary jerking of the right arm with simultaneous right-sided facial grimacing, occurring 20-40 times daily. His community neurologist diagnosed simple partial seizures (focal aware seizures) from presumed temporal lobe epilepsy based on a routine EEG showing 'mild temporal slowing' and an MRI reported as 'possible hippocampal signal change.' He was started on levetiracetam, then carbamazepine was added, then lacosamide — with no improvement in seizure frequency. Over the past 2 months, his wife reports progressive memory impairment (forgets recent conversations, gets lost driving familiar routes to work), personality change (increasingly irritable and suspicious, accused her of hiding things), sleep disturbance with violent dream enactment episodes (RBD-like behavior), and 5 kg unintentional weight loss. The brief involuntary arm/face episodes now occur 30-50 times daily. He was referred to this center for further evaluation of drug-resistant epilepsy.

neurological_exam.additional: Awareness and speech preserved during the 4 witnessed episodes; no postictal confusion or weakness afterwards.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose normal bilaterally. Heel-to-shin normal. No dysmetria.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: CN II-XII intact. No facial asymmetry between episodes. Pupils equal and reactive. Visual fields full.
neurological_exam.gait: Normal gait. No ataxia. Tandem gait normal.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert but slow to respond. Oriented to person and place but not to date (states the wrong month). MMSE 22/30 (lost points: date -1, day of week -1, delayed recall 0/3 -3, serial sevens -3). Slow processing speed. Unable to perform multi-step calculations (a math teacher who cannot do serial 7s). Affect somewhat flat.
neurological_exam.motor: During the examination, 4 brief (2-3 second) episodes of right arm extension and posturing with simultaneous right facial contraction were witnessed. Between episodes, subtle right arm choreiform movements. Strength 5/5 in bilateral upper and lower extremities. No pronator drift. Normal muscle bulk and tone.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Bilateral lower extremity reflexes mildly brisk (3+). Upper extremity reflexes 2+ and symmetric. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch, pinprick, vibration, and proprioception in all extremities.
